  ‘1  ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins; and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Susan Duenas, Public
  Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Parker Davis, Media Technician;
  Matt Myerhoff, Media Information Officer; Christina Munoz, Deputy City Clerk; Tyler
  Eaton, Senior Flaming; Salvador Lopez, Interim Assistant Planning Director; and Luis
  Flores, Public Safety Coordinator

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Dane Skophammer led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT
JLinn
  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 4:30 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8 and 54956.9, with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council discussed
  the items on the Closed Session agenda and took no reportable action.

  REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  October 18, 2024.

  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda, hearing Item No. 6.A. before Item No. 4.A, and adjoum in
  memory of Robert Hart and Felicia Hudson. The motion carried unanimously.

  ITEM 1  CONSENT CALENDAR

  City Clerk Pettijohn provided clarification on procedures for public comment on
  the Consent Calendar.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment on the Consent Calendar items.

  .J  Andy Lyon provided comments on Item No. l.B.6.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 28, 2024
  Page 3 of 13

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  Item Nos. 1.B.5. and 1.B.6. were pulled by the Council.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item Nos. 1.B.5. and 1.B.6. The motion
  carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Waive Further Reading
  Recommended Action: After the City Attorney has read the title, waive full
  reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first
  reading and/or second reading and adoption.
  2.  Approve Warrants
  Recommended Action: Allow and approve warrant demand numbers
  73861-74020 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City
  Manager to pay out the funds to each of the claimants listed in Warrant
  Register No. 756 in the amount of the warrant appearing opposite their
  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $3,158,008.68. City of Malibu payroll check number 5486-5487 and
  ACH deposits were issued in the amount of $437,903.70.
  3.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the September 4, 2024
  Special meeting and September 9, 2024 Regular meeting.
  4.  Investment Report for the Month Ending September 30, 2024
  Recommended Action: Receive the Investment Report for the month
  ending September 30, 2024.

  The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  5.  Amendment with California Skateparks
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 4
  to the Professional Services Agreement with California Skateparks in the
  amount of $29,100 for City design services and $50,400 for design services
  related to the 600 Spring Settlement Agreement.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the report.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a
  motion to authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 4 to the
  Professional Services Agreement with California Skateparks in the amount
   Malibu City Council

  Page 4 of 13

  of $29,100 for City design services and $50,400 for design services related
  to the 600 Spring Settlement Agreement. The motion carried unanimously.

  6.  Professional Services Agreements for Contract Planning Services
  Recommended Action: l) Authorize the Mayor to execute a professional
  services agreement with 4Leaf, Inc. for contract planning services; 2)
  Authorize the Mayor to execute a professional services agreement with
  Capstone City Planning for contract planning services; and 3) AuthOrize the
  Mayor to execute a professional services agreement with CSG Consultants,
  Inc. for contract planning services.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  MOTION  Mayor Stewart moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion to:
  1) authorize the Mayor to execute a professional services agreement with
  4Leaf, Inc. for contract planning services; 2) authorize the Mayor to execute
  a professional services agreement with Capstone City Planning for contract
  planning services; and 3) authorize the Mayor to execute a professional
  services agreement with CSG Consultants, Inc. for contract planning
  services. The motion carried unanimously.

  ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Presentation of Commendation to Tom Schaar in Recognition of his Silver Medal
  in Skateboarding at the 2024 Summer Olympics

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins presented the commendation to Tom Schaar.

  Mr. Schaar thanked the Council for the recognition.

  ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  E. Barry Haldeman, Malibu Arts Commission, discussed the comrhunity lands
  proj ect. He stated he was a member of the Malibu Film Society and recommended
  the Council consider including a performing arts center and movie theater in the
  community lands proj ect.

  City Manager McClary stated he attended a Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) Master
  Plan Feasibility Study meeting. He stated the next PCH Master Plan Feasibility
  Study meeting was tentatively scheduled for December 11, 2024. He discussed the
  recent public safety power shutoff (PSPS) event and the staff response procedures
  for PSPS events. He announced the Los Angeles County Office of Education
  (LACOE) committee hearings on the City’s school district separation petition on
  November 8, 2024 in the SM-MUSD Board Room, and on November l3, 2024 at
S  Malibu High School (MHS). He announced the 11-day vote center for the
  November 5, 2024 election was open at City Hall. He announced City Hall would
  be closed on Monday, November 11, 2024 for Veterans Day and the Regular City
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 28, 2024
  Page 5 of 13

  Council meeting would be held on Tuesday, November l2, 2024. He discussed
  plans for implementation for the speed cameras on PCH and announced a request
  for proposals had been issued. He announced 4—day vote centers would be open at
  the Christian Science Church, MHS, and the Topanga Library. He announced
  November 8, 2024 was the deadline to submit a Flaming Verification application
  to rebuild a non-conforming structure destroyed in the Woolsey Fire. He stated he
  attended a Las Virgenes-Malibu Council of Governments (COG) meeting and the
  League of Califomia Cities Annual Conference with all of the Department Heads.
  He stated he attended the media event at the Ghost Tires memorial on October 18,
  . 2024.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, discussed a
  burglary on October l7, 2024 on Malibu Colony Road. He discussed rescheduling
  the overnight crime suppression deputies to patrol during business hours to address
  theft issues reported by the business community. He discussed an incident they
  responded to at Pavilions and how they apprehended the suspect. He described an
  incident on October 9, 2024 where a Volunteer on Patrol (VOP) received a report
  of a burglary, identified the burglar’s vehicle and reported it to the Sheriffs
  Department and Sheriff Deputies apprehended the suspect. He read a statement
  from The Malibu Times regarding plans for a memorial for the four Pepperdine
  students killed on PCH last October. He discussed the Malibu Half Marathon over
  the weekend and stated there were no incidents.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Sergeant Soderlund discussed how
  residents and business oWners could register their security cameras with the Lost
  Hills Sheriff Stations real time crime center.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Sergeant Soderlund stated the
  emergency operations bureau would be monitoring social media and events after
  the election and the department would be on tactical alert.

RECESS  At 6:27 p.m., Mayor Stewart recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 6:33
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.

  MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to consider developing a performing arts center on the City’s La Paz Parcel C.

  The Council discussed the motion and directed questions to staff.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved to direct staff to work with the La Paz design team
  on a potential design for a performing arts center on the City’s La Paz Parcel C.

  The seconder accepted the amendment.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff and commissioners.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Silverstein moved to direct staff to work with the La Paz design
  team and a Malibu Arts Commission Ad Hoc Committee on a potential design for
  a performing arts center on the City’s La Paz Parcel C.

  The maker and the seconder accepted the amendment.

  The motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved to bring back an item to consider repaying
  Measure M funds used to purchase the Ioki and Triangle lots.

  The motion died on the floor due to lack of a second.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to authorize hiring a
  proj ect manager for the Malibu Community Lands proj ect.
RECESS  At 9:20 p.m., Mayor Stewart recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 9:33
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.
MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to hear Item Nos. 7.A., 7.B. and 7.C. before Item No. 4.A.

  The motion was withdrawn.

ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Barbara Adler was not present at the time of the hearing.

  Erik Ran was not present at the time of the hearing.

  Dru Ann Jacobson deferred time to Sherman Baylin.

  Sherman Baylin discussed her support for sports field and a skate park. She
  discussed the City’s Mission Statement and the importance of having open spaces
  for the residents.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 28, 2024
  Page 8 of 13

  Joshua Torres, Southern California Edison, discussed the recent PSPS event and
  efforts to reduce the impact and scope of PSPS events.

  The Council directed questions regarding PSPS events and procedures to Mr.
  Torres.

  Jefferson Wagner discussed the electric circuits in the City. He discussed allowable
  uses for library set-aside funds. He suggested using library funds to help develop
  the Heathercliff lot.

  Joan Murray deferred time to Jo Drummond.

  Jo Drummond discussed the Form 496 flled by Moving California Forward for
  expenditures in support of Councilmember Grisanti.  She discussed the
  contributions reported on the form. She discussed the mailers and text messages
  sent by Moving California Forward and questioned if all the expenditures were
  being properly reported. She discussed her support for Councilmember Silverstein
  and Councilmember Uhring.

  Colin Drummond discussed his volunteering in the community. He expressed his
  support for Councilmember Silverstein and Councilmember Uhring.

  Tiffany Murray discussed the City’s mission and expressed her support for
  Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember Uhring, and Andy Lyon. She
  discussed the Malibu Inn Motel hearing.

  Howard Rudzki stated it was also important to support the cultural arts with the
  community lands proj ect.

  Kevin Shenkman discussed PSPS events and stated Los Angeles Department of
  Water and Power (LADWP) did not shut off power due to weather events. He
  suggested looking into contracting with LADWP for power service.

  Andy Lyon discussed the Moving California Forward Form 496 filing and stated
  he had spent $60 on his campaign. He discussed previous surveys regarding the
  community lands and how the most recent survey allowed participation from non-
  residents. He discussed how City Hall was previously a performing arts center and
  suggested renting more office space at the La Paz shopping center. He discussed
  using the property with a transportation obligation for skateboarding and
  repurposing the Malibu Playhouse.

  Crytal Falls suggested creating a roundabout on PCH and having more horse and
  walking paths instead of cars.

ITEM 4.B.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Grisanti explained that candidates are prohibited from
  communicating with or coordinating with political action committees (PAC). He
  stated he had not communicated with or coordinated with any PAC.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins discussed the city limits and how the Malibu community
  expands beyond those limits. She discussed how non-residents who participated in
  the community land process were part of the Malibu community. She stated she
  attended the Malibu Pie Festival.

  Councilmember Uhring encouraged the residents to vote in the November 4, 2024
  election.

  Councilmember Silverstein encouraged the residents to vote in the November 4,
  2024 election.

  Mayor Stewart discussed the high voter turnout rate in Malibu. He stated he
  attended the Malibu Pie Festival and the Malibu Moves race event at Zuma. He
  commended the race organizers.

  Councilmember Grisanti stated he attended the Malibu Pie Festival.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
